g.text: N1 [Context]
LSH binary fingerprints for similarity search
Binary fingerprints from locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) are
fundamental to large-scale similarity search, enabling efficient
duplicate detection, semantic retrieval, and cross-service threat
intelligence sharing (Thakur et al., 2021;…
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Binary fingerprints from locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) are fundamental to large-scale similarity search, enabling efficient duplicate detection, semantic retrieval, and cross-service threat intelligence sharing (Thakur et al., 2021; Gill et al., 2025).

g.text: N2 [Prior_Work : ANCHOR]
SimHash: Hamming approximates cosine
SimHash (Charikar, 2002) produces compact binary codes where
Hamming distance approximates cosine similarity, making it widely
adopted for applications where raw text cannot be shared across
organizational boundaries.
g.title: N2 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) SimHash (Charikar, 2002) produces compact binary codes where Hamming distance approximates cosine similarity, making it widely adopted for applications where raw text cannot be shared across organizational boundaries.

g.text: N3 [Limitation]
SimHash collision curve leaks distance
However, this similarity-preserving property is a double-edged
sword: the collision probability P(s) = (1 + s)/2 leaks distance
information, enabling attackers to estimate pairwise similarities
from fingerprint comparisons.
g.title: N3 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, this similarity-preserving property is a double-edged sword: the collision probability P(s) = (1 + s)/2 leaks distance information, enabling attackers to estimate pairwise similarities from fingerprint comparisons.

g.text: N4 [Context]
Cross-service telemetry: privacy concern
This privacy vulnerability is particularly concerning for
cross-service telemetry sharing, where fingerprints are released
across compliance boundaries.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) This privacy vulnerability is particularly concerning for cross-service telemetry sharing, where fingerprints are released across compliance boundaries.

g.text: N5 [Context]
Adversary triangulates similarities
An adversary observing fingerprint comparisons can triangulate to estimate
original embedding similarities (Riazi et al., 2016), potentially revealing
sensitive information about the underlying data.
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=1) An adversary observing fingerprint comparisons can triangulate to estimate original embedding similarities (Riazi et al., 2016), potentially revealing sensitive information about the underlying data.

g.text: N6 [Prior_Work]
RR + noise injection prior approaches
Prior work has explored randomized response (Erlingsson et al.,
2014; Gill et al., 2025) and noise injection for fingerprint
privacy, but these approaches face fundamental limitations:
randomized response requires extreme bit flipping for…
g.title: N6 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Prior work has explored randomized response (Erlingsson et al., 2014; Gill et al., 2025) and noise injection for fingerprint privacy, but these approaches face fundamental limitations: randomized response requires extreme bit flipping for privacy but destroys utility, while noise injection shows cliff-effect behavior where small noise increases cause catastrophic utility collapse.

g.text: N6lim [Limitation]
RR destroys utility; noise has cliff effect
randomized response requires extreme bit flipping for privacy but
destroys utility, while noise injection shows cliff-effect
behavior where small noise increases cause catastrophic utility
collapse.
g.title: N6lim [Limitation] (cites=0) randomized response requires extreme bit flipping for privacy but destroys utility, while noise injection shows cliff-effect behavior where small noise increases cause catastrophic utility collapse.

g.text: N7 [Method]
Propose Secure SimHash: flatten collision curve
We propose Secure SimHash, a distance-hiding fingerprint transform that
addresses these limitations by flattening collision probability curves
rather than adding noise.
g.title: N7 [Method] (cites=0) We propose Secure SimHash, a distance-hiding fingerprint transform that addresses these limitations by flattening collision probability curves rather than adding noise.

g.text: N8 [Method]
XOR k-composition: Psec→0.5 for non-neighbors
The key insight is that by composing k independent SimHash bits with XOR,
the collision probability becomes Psec(s) = 1/2 + 1/2·p(s)^k, which
approaches 0.5 for low-similarity pairs as k increases.
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) The key insight is that by composing k independent SimHash bits with XOR, the collision probability becomes Psec(s) = 1/2 + 1/2·p(s)^k, which approaches 0.5 for low-similarity pairs as k increases.

g.text: N9 [Method]
Uninformative for non-neighbors; preserves neighbors
This makes distance estimation uninformative for non-neighbors while
preserving high collision rates for true near-neighbors, enabling both
privacy and utility.
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) This makes distance estimation uninformative for non-neighbors while preserving high collision rates for true near-neighbors, enabling both privacy and utility.

g.text: C1 [Contribution]
C1: formalize privacy-utility tradeoff
We formalize the privacy-utility tradeoff for binary fingerprints
and identify the collision probability curve as the root cause of
distance leakage.
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We formalize the privacy-utility tradeoff for binary fingerprints and identify the collision probability curve as the root cause of distance leakage.

g.text: C2 [Contribution]
C2: Secure SimHash + theory
We propose Secure SimHash with theoretical analysis showing how
k-composition with XOR flattens collision curves for non-neighbors
while preserving near-neighbor detection.
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose Secure SimHash with theoretical analysis showing how k-composition with XOR flattens collision curves for non-neighbors while preserving near-neighbor detection.

g.text: C3 [Contribution]
C3: dominates Pareto on BEIR Quora
We demonstrate empirically on BEIR Quora that Secure SimHash
dominates the privacy-utility Pareto frontier, achieving
AUC@0.5=0.463 (near random-guess) at Recall@10=0.780,
significantly outperforming randomized response and noise…
g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) We demonstrate empirically on BEIR Quora that Secure SimHash dominates the privacy-utility Pareto frontier, achieving AUC@0.5=0.463 (near random-guess) at Recall@10=0.780, significantly outperforming randomized response and noise injection baselines.
